EXTRA CLASS · COLORS

Every color, with its lesson on the card.

The color deck: eleven first colors walk in file order — red to gold, the colors a child names first — and then the deck grows up with four shades that are made, not found, each with its own mixing recipe. Every lesson below is a kid-followable guide, right on this page.

HOW THIS CLASS WORKS

Every color — with a lesson on its card.

The Colors class is a bonus class, kept beside the main learning path like the Animal Categories and the Doctor Visit: the regular classes stay the core sequence, and this one is for the days when somebody asks what color is that? Fifteen spotter sheets — eleven first colors and four make-it-yourself shades — each one a two-by-two sheet of four labeled things in one color. Sixty labeled pictures in one deck: the red apple, the yellow sun, the grey elephant, the gold honey pot, and every square between. Each card opens a simple lesson a kid can follow: what the color is, where it hides in your house, and one way to hunt it tonight.

The deck runs in file order on purpose. It starts with red — usually the first color word a child learns — and walks through blue, yellow, green, orange, purple, pink, brown, black, grey and gold, ending on the shiny treasure card. Then the deck grows up: four shades that are not found but made — light blue, navy, peach and lavender — each with its own mixing recipe, for bigger spotters.

The eleven colors a child names first, in the deck’s own order — red to gold, one card per page. Every simple lesson is right here on this page: the original card beside the kid-followable guide.

MORE COLORS (AGES 4-5)

More colors (ages 4-5).

Four shades for bigger spotters — and a bigger idea: these colors are not found, they are MADE. Light blue is blue plus white, navy is blue gone dark, peach is orange gone soft, lavender is purple gone pale. Every shade lesson teaches its recipe — and mixing them for real is the whole game.

Light BlueNavyPeachLavender
THE CLASS GAME

The Color Hunt: turn the house into the deck.

Pick one card — say, the red one — and hunt its color all day: clothes, cups, cars, cushions, the crust on toast. Every find is called out loud: red car! red cup! red sock! Count the finds as you go and try to beat yesterday’s total. Then swap cards tomorrow — gold days hunt crowns and door handles, grey days hunt elephants and pavement. The house reshuffles itself into a new color lesson every single morning — and the day’s winner picks dinner’s plate color, which is exactly as powerful as it sounds.

SAME COLOR, TWO NAMES

Grey and gray. Both are right.

Colors carry their names across oceans like passports, and this class says so out loud. The card says grey — the UK spelling — while families in the US write gray: same gentle elephant-cloud color, two spellings, both correct. The glossy purple vegetable is an eggplant in the US and an aubergine in the UK. Whichever your family says, your child hears both — and learns early that colors, like words, come in families.

SUPPORTING RESOURCE

Print the color cards.

Every lesson has a matching flashcard in the library: the original artwork as a printable card with a download button and short notes for grown-ups. Keep the deck in the play corner — all fifteen colors, sorted and ready.

Age ranges are a guide, not a test. The age pill on every card is an honest hint, not a rule: the eleven first colors ride Ages 2+ — they are pointing-and-naming cards, the first words a toddler learns — and the four shades ride Ages 4–5, because each one is a mixing recipe with two ingredients to hold in mind. Any card a child loves is the right card today.

THE ROOM THAT PAINTS WITH THESE COLORS

Step into the Art Room.

The Colors class hunts every shade the house hides — and the school’s Art Room is where those colors become things: twenty-seven supply cards from crayons to watercolors, each with its own make-it activity. Mix two colors on the palette card, paint a bright background with the brush, dab clouds with cotton balls — every supply has a short page, a full lesson and a printable card, and the whole room rides on ages 2–5. Naming colors here, making with them there: the two shelves finish each other.

TEACHER’S LESSON

How this class is taught.

By the end of this class: your child has met all 15 cards in Colors & Shades, said each word with you and tried one small activity from the lesson.

  1. 01
    Welcome

    “Hello! Today we are learning about Colors & Shades. We have 15 cards, and we will look at them one at a time.”

    How: Sit side by side with the cards in front of you. Keep your voice warm and unhurried, and let your child touch the cards.

  2. 02
    Card 1 · Red

    “Red! The apple is red, the fire truck is red, the ladybug is red, the strawberry is red. Can you find something red in this room? Look — your cup is red too!”

    How: Red hunt: walk the house naming every red thing you pass. Ten finds and the hunt is won — and dinner plates, door frames and book spines all count. Red is everywhere once you start looking.

  3. 03
    Card 2 · Blue

    “Blue! The whale is blue, the umbrella is blue, the balloon is blue, the bluebird is blue. What else is blue? The sky! Look up — the whole sky is blue today.”

    How: Balloon blue: blow up one blue balloon (or draw one) and keep it off the floor with color call-outs — every tap needs the word "blue!" said first. Wiggly, giggly, and the word sticks.

  4. 04
    Card 3 · Yellow

    “Yellow! The sun is yellow, the banana is yellow, the duck is yellow, the star is yellow. Can you quack like the yellow duck? Can you stretch tall like the yellow sun?”

    How: Banana count: peel a real banana at snack time and say "yellow" three times on the way to the first bite — then count the bites. Snack math plus color naming in one go.

  5. 05
    Card 4 · Green

    “Green! The leaf is green, the frog is green, the cucumber is green, the turtle is green. Hop like the green frog! Crawl slow like the green turtle! Snack time: let’s crunch a green cucumber.”

    How: Frog hops: every time you say "green", your child does one frog hop across the room. Four squares, four hops — and a cucumber crunch at the finish line. Colors plus wiggles, both won.

  6. 06
    Card 5 · Orange

    “Orange! The orange is orange, the tiger is orange, the carrot is orange, the fox is orange. An orange you can eat, a tiger you can roar at! Can you prowl like the orange tiger?”

    How: Tiger stripes: tape or draw paper stripes on a orange t-shirt and prowl the hallway on all fours, roaring "ORANGE!" at each corner. The fox trot home is the cool-down.

  7. 07
    Card 6 · Purple

    “Purple! The grapes are purple, the eggplant is purple, the butterfly is purple, the plum is purple. Snack time: purple grapes! Garden time: let’s find a purple flower.”

    How: Grape counting: pile ten purple grapes and count them before eating — one to ten, one purple at a time. Then flap arms like the purple butterfly between every third grape. Counts, colors, wiggles.

  8. 08
    Card 7 · Pink

    “Pink! The flamingo is pink, the cupcake is pink, the flower is pink, the pig is pink. Stand on one leg like the pink flamingo! Snuffle like the pink pig!”

    How: Flamingo stand: hold up the card and everyone balances on one leg like the flamingo — the last one standing picks the next color card. Giggly balance practice with a color name attached.

  9. 09
    Card 8 · Brown

    “Brown! The bear is brown, the pretzel is brown, the mushroom is brown, the coffee cup is brown. Hug your teddy — is your teddy brown too? Grown-ups: whose cup looks like the coffee cup?”

    How: Teddy picnic: every brown toy comes to the picnic blanket, and each one gets a "brown" said out loud on arrival. The pretzel square gets a real pretzel if the pantry cooperates.

  10. 10
    Card 9 · Black

    “Black! The penguin is black, the piano is black, the cat is black, the tire is black. Waddle like the black penguin! Tinkle pretend piano keys! Vroom goes the tire!”

    How: Penguin waddle race: waddle across the room with feet together saying "black, black, black" — then three pretend piano plinks at the finish. The cat gets a quiet, sneaky lap back.

  11. 11
    Card 10 · Grey

    “Grey! The elephant is grey, the cloud is grey, the rock is grey, the koala is grey. Stomp slow like the grey elephant! Yawn like the sleepy grey koala! What does the cloud do? Float!”

    How: Elephant stomp: slow, heavy, grey stomps across the room — then float to a chair like the cloud when the music stops. Loud and quiet, same color. The koala nap at the end is mandatory.

  12. 12
    Card 11 · Gold

    “Gold! The crown is gold, the sunflower is gold, the trophy is gold, the honey pot is gold. Gold is yellow’s shiny cousin! Who wears a crown? Who wins a trophy? YOU do — every color you name is a win!”

    How: Golden treasure hunt: hide one gold thing (a spoon, a button, the card itself) and hunt it like treasure — the finder is crowned with paper and wears it to lunch. Sunflower snack: seeds, counted by twos for the older kids.

  13. 13
    Card 12 · Light Blue

    “Light blue! It is blue plus white — sky blue! The kite is light blue, the raindrop is light blue, the helmet is light blue, the cloud is light blue. Who has ridden a bike with a helmet on?”

    How: Mix it for real: blue paint plus white paint, stirred slow — light blue arrives and it is MAGIC every time. Then paint a raindrop or cut a paper kite from the fresh batch.

  14. 14
    Card 13 · Navy

    “Navy! It is blue with a little black — night blue! The whale is navy, the moon is navy, the bow tie is navy, the cap is navy. Navy is the color of sailors’ clothes — that is HOW it got its name!”

    How: Day and night: hold the blue card and the navy card side by side — day sky, night sky. Then draw one sky in each color on one folded paper. Two blues, two times of day, one artist.

  15. 15
    Card 14 · Peach

    “Peach! It is orange plus white and a hug of pink. The peach is peach, the seashell is peach, the kitten is peach, the ballet slipper is peach. Soft like a kitten’s ear — can you stroke your arm that gently?”

    How: Fuzzy feel: peaches are fuzzy — pass a real one around and name the color with eyes closed, by touch. Then the whole family tiptoes like ballet dancers in peach slippers.

  16. 16
    Card 15 · Lavender

    “Lavender! It is purple plus white — pale purple, like the flower. The lavender is lavender, the fairy is lavender, the teapot is lavender, the butterfly is lavender. Smell the word: lavender smells like Grannie’s drawer!”

    How: Smell and spell: if a lavender plant (or sachet) is nearby, smell it FIRST, then name the color — a color with a scent sticks twice as deep. Then mix purple + white paint to brew the shade at the table.

  17. 17
    Practice

    “Now you are the teacher! Pick any card and tell me what it is.”

    How: Let your child choose the card and say the word in their own way. Teaching someone else is the strongest way to remember.

  18. 18
    Check

    “Can you find Red? Now show me Brown.”

    How: A point, a fetch or the word all count as a pass. If they are unsure, name it for them and try again another day — there are no scores and no pressure.

  19. 19
    Well done

    “Well done! Today we met 15 cards. Let us look for one of them at home.”

    How: End on a win, then spot one of the words in real life today. Meeting it again in the real world is what makes it stay.

Read the script while you show the cards — the say-lines are yours to say out loud and the how-lines are the activity behind each step. Skip, shorten or repeat anything: the class bends to your child, never the other way round.
